newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends higher but off peaks as crude di.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends higher but off peaks as crude di.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended slightly higher on Monday, but off levels seen in early trade as crude futures dipped in the afternoon and one player sold Eurograde barge material at aggressively low prices.
Eurograde barges traded at $210 and $212 fob ARA in morning trade and at $207 and $210 fob ARA in afternoon trade.
Some players confessed to being rather puzzled by the strategy behind the player who sold at $207.
"We offered them a bid at $210 and they said they would wait for a bid above $212, the next thing we saw is that they sold at $207," said one player.
Traders were also slightly sceptical about the motives of the player buying at $212 in early trade. Many speculated the player was seeking to protect swaps positions.
"They probably sold it to set pricing levels. I wouldn't be surprised if we saw a reversal of the deal tomorrow," said one trader.
Regular barges were assessed at $202/$203 fob ARA.
Swaps were done as high as $212 on Monday, but by the close of the day they were assessed around the $210/$211 fob ARA level for April.
On the cargo front, traders said business was quiet.
The trans-Atlantic arbitrage window was just about open but traders said many players wanted it to widen a little more before organising West-bound cargoes.

"There was a lot of talk on arb opportunities this morning, but once crude headed down most people lost confidence. They see negative numbers and they get nervous," said one trader. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
